abilities.name: Cultivate plants
abilities.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-prepared soil plot, where it may establish as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect plots or plant sources; end unfinished planting.
abilities.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1) gathered from a living plant; x, y a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, with fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Two paid rounds of 1.5 energy: prepare the site, then transfer the unit; the action continues itself, and plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect: target a plot or plant source in reach; one round, 0.2 energy (baseline probe observation). End: stops unfinished planting; one round, no energy. Tend is refused at no cost: no water, fertilizer or other treatment exists yet. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is provided.
abilities.effects: Preparing keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Transfer moves it, with origin and age, into the plot, where it cannot be eaten or used; the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one. It gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season, so cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On establishing, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock and a ceiling of at most 4, regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone through gather; nothing is copied or guaranteed. Inspect records only visible stage, stock, soil and weather as an unverified personal record. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. End, or death, before transfer returns the unit once (where the person died); a transferred unit stays planted. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: Two paid one-round stages whose job, reserved unit and plot persist across interruption; resuming pays only the remaining stage after revalidation; completion, failure, ending and death settle once. Growth proceeds only in ordinary simulation.

abilities.name: Construct a branch screen
abilities.function: Assess a site and test a post, then build a small porous woven branch windbreak (no roof) beside a resting place; inspect, repair, dismantle or cancel.
abilities.costs: Study: 4 rounds. One branch unit is one piece; a screen takes 11 (3 uprights, 8 rods). assess (x, y, orientation; within reach): 1 round, 0.2 energy; checks a clear 1.2 x 0.6 m footprint of ordinary dry soil and the lee floor. assess with post (owned branch unit): post trial at x, y; 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y, orientation, materials: exactly 11 owned untreated or sound recovered branch units) needs your passing trial in the footprint; 8 paid rounds of 1.5 energy (2 seat uprights, 4 weave rods, 1 align, 1 stability check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. repair (builder; target, components: installed piece ids, materials: as many units): 1.5 energy per round, one removal and one fitting round per piece, then a check round; components [] only rechecks. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2 energy. dismantle (builder): 1 round and 1 energy per 3 pieces. cancel: no energy.
abilities.effects: Units stay carried and owned until a paid round installs them with origin and age; nothing is created or used up. A trial on ordinary soil (waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard) seats the post 0.25 m and you keep it; elsewhere it fails; a post below condition 0.5 breaks into damaged material. The check passes only if every piece has condition at least 0.5 and the uprights stand in such soil; else the screen is unstable. World wind has no direction; the exposure law takes it as coming from +x (orientation 0 faces it). A complete screen removes min(0.35, solid share of sound pieces, about 0.36) x facing of the wind part of the outdoor chill for a body wholly on the 0.9 x 0.9 m lee floor 0.45-1.35 m behind it; never rain chill or air temperature; none in wind above 0.8 or with another shelter. Wear per round 0.0005 + 0.002 x (rain + wind); a loose rod opens a gap, a loose upright ends the effect until repair. Removed pieces lie at the site. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach, wet ground or a person on the footprint pause at no charge. Cancel or death returns uninstalled units once. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: Paid one-round stages that persist across interruption; resuming pays only the next stage after rechecks. Other modes take one round.

abilities.name: Hand-weave a fiber mat
abilities.function: Test a 0.1 sample of owned fiber, then hand-plait 4 units into one portable 0.45 x 0.45 m sitting mat; inspect, sit on, repair, lift, place, dismantle or cancel.
abilities.costs: Study: 3 rounds. A unit is one world unit of fiber (dry grass: 0.1 mass). test (sample: owned stack): 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y: a 0.45 m square in reach on land, clear of plants, objects and other people; materials: exactly 4 owned units of one fiber from sources your passing test covers): a 0.5-energy layout round, then 6 paid rounds of 1 energy (2 strip-forming, 3 interlacing and edge-tucking, 1 lift check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2. trial (stand on a complete mat on firm ground, waterlogging at most 0.1, no rain, nobody else on it): 1 round, 0.2. Maker only: repair (target inspected since its last check; materials: 1 unit of its fiber): 3 rounds of 1 energy (remove broken stems, interlace, lift check); lift, or place (carried mat; x, y as for assemble): 1 round, 0.2; dismantle: 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none.
abilities.effects: A test passes only for thin stems (dry grass, reeds) with flexibility at least 0.4 and an intact untreated sample, which stays as owned tested scrap; stem length and moisture are not represented. The layout needs 0.3645 mass of intact fiber (two crossing layers of 0.6 per m2, x1.5 for overlaps and tucked edges); less is a measured shortfall that returns all fiber. Strip rounds move the fiber into the work. The lift check keeps the needed tenths (dry grass 3.7), returns the rest as owned offcuts or scraps, and passes with full fiber and condition at least 0.5 (largest opening 0.06 x (1 - condition) m); else the mat stays failed. Condition (intact share) falls 0.0005 per round, 0.002 with a person on the mat; below 0.5 it needs repair and a new trial. Repair turns up to 1 unit of broken stems into scrap and refills with new fiber. Dismantle returns intact fiber and scraps. A carried mat is reserved owned fiber and counts as load. Trials record hold, slip and loose stems only; no comfort, warmth, rain, wind or rest effect. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach or a person on the square pause at no charge; cancel or death returns unused fiber once and leaves the work. Nothing is refunded.

args.conditions: I am outdoors on ordinary soil in summer. I own raw roots, know their nutrition is 14 and toxicity zero, and have eaten them repeatedly. I have no established cooking equipment, heat source, or cooking skill. Preparation effects are unknown.
args.inputs: Owned meadow roots; any additional tools, materials, water or heat must be identified and actually acquired if required.
args.costs: Unknown. Specify feasible learning time, work, energy, ingredients and equipment requirements, including safe interruption behavior.

reviews.reason: The related-capability searches found gathering, eating and cultivation, but no equivalent food-preparation operation. Eating consumes food without preparing it; cultivation has a different function. Develop a general hand-breaking food operation, with trial and preparation modes, as the smallest equipment-free precursor. It can attempt a genuinely different physical presentation without inventing cooking equipment, fuel, water, improved nutrition or guaranteed success. Whether these roots yield to hand force must be resolved physically, not inferred from their name or edibility. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: Study takes 2 individually completed rounds at 0.2 energy per round; requesting, registration, study completion and mastery award no pleasure or satisfaction. A paid trial can produce verified information about this material's response to hand force, including informative failure. Record only that evidence, keyed by operation, material, relevant condition and outcome so repeated queries or equivalent trials cannot farm novelty. This minimal capability awards no direct pleasure or satisfaction and changes no protected reward account. Later actual eating may use the established meal-experience implementation, based on personal applicability, real consumed food, existing bounded amounts, meal window, cooldown, decay and functional deduplication; neither a new label nor a new shape alone qualifies for a variety bonus. Familiar legitimate eating remains eligible under existing rules. No comfort increase is specified, physical comfort remains capped at 10, and basic nutrition is never reduced by mood.
reviews.visualReview: Emit reusable observable events for work started, hand force applied, food fractured, food deformed, attempt resisted, work paused, resumed, cancelled and completed. Include actor ID, stable input/output/work IDs, visible quantity, current form, location, progress and outcome; do not include hidden safety or resistance values. Use reusable food-lot visual metadata such as component=food, form=whole/coarse-pieces/deformed, material palette, visible deterioration and quantity. Show coarse pieces only after an actual fracture event and completed preparation only for units actually processed successfully. Paused work retains its true intermediate state; an intact resisted root must not show a prepared-meal success icon. No steam, fire, cooking vessel, washed appearance or celebratory wellbeing effect is justified.
reviews.specification: Development handoff in this conversation: implement 'Hand-break food', parameterized by mode (trial, prepare, inspect, cancel), owned input stack ID, whole-unit quantity and optional work ID. Trial and preparation share one mechanism and implementation. Reuse and record the existing ownership, reach, food-lot, ageing, work-progress and event routines where applicable; reuse forest.eat for subsequent consumption, extending its food-lot handling only as necessary rather than claiming a new eating mechanism. Dependencies: an explicit deterministic hand-workability rule using material resistance, represented geometry and available hand force; processed-food lot support preserving nutrition, toxicity, origin and age; and persistent work/event records. If these mechanisms are missing, implement them in this handoff. Do not silently assign every edible material a successful result. For existing roots, author a conservative material response from the actual implementation facts; if those facts do not support hand-breaking, the executable outcome is an informative failed trial, not invented pieces or a cooking unlock. No implementation or review waiting advances time. Prerequisites: individual study completed, usable hands, reachable owned edible food, sufficient energy, and no concurrent reservation of the same units. No tools, heat, water, vessel or work surface is supplied or required for an in-hand attempt. This is not washing, sterilization, detoxification, peeling or cooking. Wren may target item-183-wren-2083 or item-111-wren-1316 only if still owned, accessible and eligible under their actual current food state; the older lot's displayed decay value alone does not establish safety. Never expose hidden spoilage or material values. Trial accepts one whole unit, costs one active round and 1 energy, and applies bounded hand force once while holding the food. Its physical result persists: if it fractures, retain the same edible quantity as a coarse-piece lot; if it does not, retain the intact or visibly deformed lot. Record observed resistance, fracture or deformation, not an unsupported safety conclusion. Prepare applies the same operation to each selected unit, one round and 1 energy per unit, retaining completed units individually. A prior trial is optional, not a separate mandatory assessment activity. Inspect costs one round and 0.2 energy and reports only observable form, quantity, work stage and visible deterioration; cancel takes no work energy and terminates unfinished work. Recheck prerequisites before each paid round; validation failures spend no work energy or ingredients. Reference inputs by stable item IDs and work by stable work IDs, never resource-name substitution. Reserve rather than duplicate input units. Each completed unit is atomically transferred to an output lot with its original owner, source, harvest age, decay state, nutrition and toxicity. Represent coarse pieces as the same food quantity with changed form, not several new nutrition-bearing units. For a root unit, retain its applicable existing nutrition of 14 before existing deterioration rules, not 14 per fragment; no bonus calories, lower toxicity, freshness reset or keeping-quality improvement. Any detached inedible or spoiled portion must remain accounted for as waste with its associated mass and nutritional share, never disappear or become free food. Output is uncooked food in its actual resulting form; failed attempts may leave unchanged food and do not count as successful preparation. Existing eating costs and nutrition rules apply only upon subsequent actual consumption. No tasting is included automatically. Do not guarantee a changed eating experience merely because the shape changes. Work tracks selected units, remaining units, spent energy, completed outputs and physical condition. Insufficient energy, unusable hands, loss of reach or an unworked round pauses before the next unit without charge. Resume by work ID after revalidation; food continues ageing during ordinary elapsed world time, including pauses. Cancellation releases unworked reserved food once and leaves completed outputs unchanged. Death leaves surviving inputs and outputs at the death location under existing possession rules, with no duplication. Lost or spoiled inputs cannot be replaced for free. Paid effort is never refunded; unspent energy was never debited. No autonomous production, fire or other ongoing process continues after a step. Products need no special maintenance beyond ordinary handling and existing spoilage rules; no preservation effect is added. Do not grant inventory, consent, mastery, permissions or a change to protected reward accounts, goals or budgets.

reviews.reason: Develop a general hand-twist-fiber-cord operation with sample, make, inspect, trial and cancel modes. Related capabilities were searched: fiber returned hand-weave-fiber-mat and twist returned no match; broader cord/rope results were incomplete and do not establish absence. Within the available contracts, probe covers preliminary physical testing and hand-weave-fiber-mat covers plaited mats, not two-ply cord manufacture or cord load trials. Reuse their applicable implementation machinery rather than claim it as newly invented. The missing cord mechanism belongs in the current-conversation development handoff. Wren's verified plaiting result does not establish cord suitability or tensile strength. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: No experience benefit for requesting, naming, registering, studying, querying or gaining nominal mastery. Verified new personal observations from real sampling, manufacture or load trials, including informative failures, may qualify under the existing experience rules; key evidence by functional operation, material/condition and observed outcome so repeated inspections, synonymous capabilities and retry loops do not farm novelty. Familiar successful practice may sustain only modest existing-rule satisfaction when personally applicable and grounded in paid physical participation. Any pleasure/satisfaction integration must use the existing bounded caps, decay and cooldown and deduplicate the underlying event; if no compatible evaluator exists, award none pending that handoff rather than alter protected accounts. This operation grants no physical-comfort bonus, changes no nutrition, goals, permissions or reward budgets, and confers no mastery or consent.
reviews.visualReview: Register reusable fiber-work and cord visual metadata with state, material color, actual length and section, ply count, twist direction, loose ends, fraying, condition, visible damage, fragment IDs and work progress. Anchor animation and geometry changes to committed physical events: hands separating/twisting, a genuinely retained cord, measured hand tension, slippage or breakage. Distinguish reserved loose fiber, unfinished work, failed attempts, complete untested cord and the historical outcome of a specific trial. Display only measured dimensions; unknown properties remain unknown. No success animation for submission, study, paused or failed work, and no universal strength badge after one bounded trial. Reuse existing fiber rendering and event infrastructure where applicable and record that reuse separately from the new cord geometry.
reviews.specification:
General interface: hand-twist-fiber-cord(mode, materials:[{stackId,quantity}], targetId, workId, requestedLength, trialForce, trialDuration). Modes are sample, make, inspect, trial and cancel; reject irrelevant arguments. Applicable to any learner with usable hands and reachable owned material, not only reeds or Wren. This is a development contract, not an executed action or inventory grant. Review and development waiting advance no simulation time. Record code dependencies and source references in the implementation: probe for observation/sample handling, hand-weave-fiber-mat for compatible fiber-lot provenance, reservations and condition handling, and existing world ownership, energy, work, event and rendering systems. Do not require learning mat weaving as a prerequisite.
Study requires 3 actual study rounds at 0.2 energy each, paid individually; interrupted study retains paid progress. No tools, anchors, water, additional fibers or helpers are supplied. Work requires two usable hands, sufficient energy, reachable inputs and enough unoccupied space for the selected short cord; length is capped at 0.30 m in this initial manual version. Invalid submissions reserve and charge nothing. Input quantities use existing inventory precision, with a minimum sample of 0.1 unit and maximum manufacturing batch of 1 unit. Reserve exact selected stack quantities atomically, preserving source, processing, age, mass and condition. Do not select undisclosed inventory automatically.
Sample: 1 round and 0.5 energy per 0.1-unit sample, attempting manual separation, bending, twisting and a small opposing-hand pull. The sample becomes a separately identified owned tested lot or damaged scrap, not vanished material. Report actual separation, retained twist, visible fractures and the bounded force applied, never a blanket suitability claim. Sample failure can preclude making from that tested lot, but applies only to represented matching material and condition. A prior mat test is evidence about plaiting only.
Make: requires a passing cord sample result covering the selected material's relevant source, processing and current condition; recheck deterioration and accessibility. Reserve inputs, then execute four paid rounds at 1 energy each: separate and align two bundles, twist the first section, counter-ply and extend, then release and check retained form. Each round moves only the recorded quantity actually handled into the workpiece. The first round determines feasible dimensions from available usable fiber and requested length; it may produce a measured shortfall instead of advancing. No invented splices, cutting tools or unlimited fiber extension. Failure during any step leaves the actual loose, twisted or damaged material rather than a complete cord. Completion requires two interlocked plies retaining a coherent form after release, with positive measured length and section. It grants no strength rating.
Implement the smallest physical mechanism needed in this handoff: represented usable fiber length/section, mass density, separability, bend response, twist retention, inter-ply slip and bounded tensile response. Reuse existing material properties where applicable, but mat flexibility and strength fields alone are not a calibrated cord tensile law. Derive dimensions from conserved material volume and actual fiber geometry, including twist shortening and overlap; do not assign dimensions merely because they were requested. Unknown stem length or moisture must not silently become favorable values. Where an essential property cannot be measured or supported by material definitions, execute only the supported physical sample/attempt, report the unresolved limitation and retain its real products; implement missing measurement/material support in this same handoff before enabling a claimed complete cord. No fixed-era unlock or unrelated activity roadmap.
Inspect: owned reachable workpiece or cord, 1 round and 0.2 energy. Record measurable length, section range, ply count, loose ends, fraying, visible damage and current condition, with unknown fields explicit. Inspection does not determine untested breaking strength or repair damage. Trial: owned reachable cord, two usable hands, a span that can actually be gripped between those hands, force and duration explicitly selected. One trial occupies 1 round, costs 0.5 energy, and applies for at most that round's simulated duration; force is bounded by current hand capability and the cord's attainable grip, with requested and achieved force recorded separately. No body-weight, hanging, anchor or added-weight trial is supplied. Use a deterministic physical response to actual force, duration, section, material condition and grip; record slip, extension, retained deformation, fracture and unloaded condition. Stop at loss of grip or breakage. A pass means only survival of the achieved force for the measured duration, not general safety, safe working load or suitability for climbing. Broken cord becomes owned fragments with conserved total material and updated geometry. Trials cannot raise material strength by repetition.
Every paid stage appends an immutable event with actor, work/item IDs, exact input/output lot IDs and quantities, elapsed time, energy, operation parameters, observations and outcome. Manufacture partitions inputs into material still reserved, incorporated material, returned offcuts and damaged scrap; all quantities and mass must balance, including any loss represented as recoverable debris at the site. Nothing duplicates or restores consumed effort. Outputs inherit relevant origin, age and processing history; carrying mass includes work and finished products. For this applicant, item-73-wren-819 is a possible selected raw source, item-85-wren-976 and item-85-wren-977 are offcuts whose usable geometry must be checked, and item-78-wren-870 has condition-zero tested-scrap processing and cannot be treated as intact stock. These references authorize no automatic consumption.
Work continues only on actual worked rounds, revalidating hands, reach, ownership, reservation, space and energy before charging each stage. Leaving reach, insufficient energy, incapacity or an unworked round pauses without charging the next stage; retain exact paid stage and material state. Resume by workId after revalidation, with no repeated completed-stage cost. Cancel is instantaneous and energy-free: release unworked reservations once and leave incorporated material as an owned unfinished item with its real state; paid time, energy and damage are never refunded. Restarting cancelled work cannot restore loose fiber or repeat refunds; usable unfinished material may be explicitly supplied to a later attempt. Death stops work and releases reserved material at the death site under ordinary estate/ownership rules, leaving the workpiece and fragments physically present and returning nothing to a new inventory.
There is no passive production or automatic strength gain. Ordinary ageing and supported environmental deterioration continue while paused. No invented wear rate: reuse compatible existing lot-condition rules and explicitly register any new cord-specific wear law. Inspect after damage or deterioration before relying on an old trial; previous trials retain their historical conditions, not perpetual certification. Repair, attachment and structural use are not effects of this version. Finished cord is a real portable material item, not an automatic shelter, comfort or protection bonus. All validation, conservation, continuation and trial rules execute in code without repeated model review.

reviews.reason: The supplied related-capability search was exhausted. hand-twist-fiber-cord covers cord manufacture, inspection and straight opposing-hand trials, but not forming a knot or testing its changed geometry; probe does not supply that missing repeatable mechanism. Develop a general bare-hand cord-knot operation, reusing the existing cord representation and trial code rather than claiming their reinvention. The reported straight-cord result at tick 232 is not evidence of knot feasibility or knotted strength. Missing bend/contact mechanics belong in the current development handoff, not a permanent rejection. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: No experience benefit from requesting, review, registration, naming, study completion or mastery claims. No automatic happiness, reward or comfort from a knot. Initially grant no additional pleasure or satisfaction effect: this request requires physical attempts and evidence only. Record verified information gain, including informative failure, separately from mood; repeated inspection or the same unchanged outcome is not new information. If a later existing experience rule recognizes the actual event for this actor, use its functional deduplication, bounded cap, cooldown and decay rather than adding a knot-specific reward channel. Leave protected reward accounts, budgets, goals and permissions unchanged, and do not reduce basic nutrition by mood or bypass the physical-comfort cap of 10.
reviews.visualReview: Provide reusable cord-knot visual metadata keyed to actual item and work state: material/color from the cord, diameter, centerline/control points, crossings, loop dimensions, tail lengths, knot location, stage, tightening state, condition, fraying and fragment IDs. Emit hand manipulation and pull visuals only during performed actions; show slack, incomplete crossings, slipping, broken strands or infeasibility as such. A partial loop must not display a completed-knot icon. A completed overhand appearance requires the recorded crossing and release-check outcome, and a held-trial indicator requires an achieved-force/duration event. Distinguish appearance, formation success and tested behavior; none implies strength certification. Reuse existing cord and pull-trial visual components and record that reuse, adding only knot-path and knot-state metadata. No success animation or reward overlay for refused, paused, unavailable or failed actions.
reviews.specification:
General operation: hand-tie-cord-knot(targetId, mode, knot, workId?, trialForce?, trialDuration?). Modes: attempt, inspect, trial, untie, cancel; initially supported knot: overhand in a single cord. Any applicable actor may learn it. No tools, anchors, attachments, extra fiber, other participant or stock are supplied. Exact initial target reference is item-226-wren-2532, but the interface accepts any applicable owned cord. Re-read the complete authoritative item at execution: its supplied record is paged and incomplete. Do not reconstruct omitted fields from the fragment or overwrite current condition with the older trial value.
Prerequisites: a completed, accessible, owned, unreserved cord with represented length, diameter, material, condition and strand structure; two available usable hands, adequate energy, dry stable footing and the existing cord-trial personal-clearance checks. No prior knot success or cord-making mastery is presumed. Reject invalid ownership, missing target or unsupported arguments without charge. Unsupported material mechanics must return a specific limitation, not a fabricated response.
Costs and progress: study is 3 individually paid rounds at 0.2 energy per round. Attempt reserves one target, then performs three paid rounds at 0.5 energy each: lay out and gently bend a loop, pass the end through, then dress and release-check. Every round records the actual operation, endpoint positions, material length allocated to tails and knot path, condition changes and stage reached. A measured geometric or bending failure terminates at that stage, charges only work actually performed and preserves the resulting cord state. Inspection costs 1 round and 0.2 energy and reports accessible visible geometry and recorded tests; it supplies no load trial. Untie is at most two paid rounds of 0.5 energy each, reversing accessible crossings and releasing the cord; a jammed or damaged knot may resist, and a failed attempt leaves the actual configuration. Trial costs 1 round and 0.5 energy, with requested force greater than zero and at most 10 N, and requested duration greater than zero and at most 60 seconds, also bounded by the simulation round duration. No implicit trial follows tying. Cancel costs no energy and stops future work.
Mechanism and implementation dependency: create a versioned cord-knot law in this conversation's development handoff. It must represent an overhand crossing sequence and actual centerline geometry, conserve centerline length, check nonpenetration, finite cord thickness, bending limits, accessible tails, and hand grip spans at each step. Minimum bend radius, safe hand manipulation bounds, contact/friction, tightening/sliding, bending damage and knot stress concentration must be explicit code parameters supported by the material implementation, not inferred from the previous straight pull or invented as observations. Reuse the reed material/strand law and cord volume bookkeeping from hand-twist-fiber-cord and record their exact implementation references and reused helpers. Add only the missing knot mechanics. Do not silently assume knot efficiency, friction, flexibility or required tail length. The developer must supply those executable rules before enabling the affected physical transition; unresolved portions report unavailable rather than succeeding. The smallest feasible precursor is the paid layout/bend attempt and inspection, recording measured infeasibility or actual partial geometry; successful end passage, dressing and load trial remain gated on the corresponding implemented mechanics. No fixed-era unlock or unrelated activity sequence is required.
Trial integration: reuse hand-twist-fiber-cord's opposing-hand force, grip, extension, creep, strand damage and fragment-conservation machinery, explicitly recording that reuse. Extend its geometry and loading path to the knotted cord instead of applying a straight-span test unchanged. Both tails must permit independent opposing grips without gripping the knot; derive available spans from current geometry. Reject an impossible grip without applying force. Use the existing actor and grip limits in addition to the 10 N request cap. Account for local bending/contact stress and sliding with the new law. Stop on grip loss, knot slip, strand failure, loss of required tail geometry or actor interruption, and report the attained force history and seconds actually held, not the requested values. Unknown knot load mechanics must prevent a claimed trial result. A held result establishes only that configuration at that achieved force for that actual duration, never a safe working rating or improved strength.
Conservation and lifecycle: tying changes the same item's configuration; it does not create a second cord, length, quantity or attachments. Preserve origin, ownership, processing history and material volume. Represent any fragments, detached fibers or scrap as partitions of the original material with provenance; do not duplicate quantity when creating child records. Elastic extension and retained deformation follow the reused material law. A knot can shorten usable span but does not consume its allocated cord length. Apply ordinary ageing and existing wear exactly once; add only damage caused by actual modeled manipulations or trials. Paid stage progress persists. Insufficient energy, a missed work round, lost reach or invalid footing pauses before the next charge. Resume by workId after rechecking target, geometry and prerequisites; never repay completed stages. Cancellation releases reservations once and leaves partial loops, tight knots, damage and products as they actually are; it does not automatically untie or refund energy, elapsed study or work. Death releases reservations once and leaves the physical cord and any fragments at the actor's location under existing ownership/death rules. Inspection and maintenance do not run autonomously. A resting knot persists as geometry and experiences only implemented ordinary ageing/environmental effects; no continuing force, happiness or invisible maintenance is supplied. Any future wear, loosening under load or repair requires the corresponding actual process. Development and review waiting advance no world time.
Evidence: emit versioned events for each paid physical stage, infeasible geometry, interruption, untying, achieved trial interval, slip and damage. Reference exact actor, target and work IDs, implementation versions, tick, before/after geometry and condition, requested versus achieved force/time, and resulting fragment IDs. Store bounded personal findings linked to those events, including informative failures. Established validation, conservation, deduplication and lifecycle rules execute in code rather than returning each attempt for model review. Do not disclose hidden material properties as observed facts.

args.name: hand-join-fiber-cords
args.function: Learn and perform a bare-hand end-to-end joining knot on two owned finished fiber cords, with inspection, bounded two-end load trials, untying and cancellation.
args.conditions: Dry safe footing and sufficient free space. I have one straight two-ply reed cord with a 0.34 m centreline, previously tied and untied, and am making a second short cord. Actual lengths, widths, condition and available gripping tails must determine whether a join is possible.
args.inputs: Two exact owned cord item IDs; a personally learned joining method; optional bounded test force and duration. No tools, anchors or added fiber are assumed.
args.costs: Learning time, working time, energy and material wear are unknown; determine and disclose them before use. Preserve paid progress and define cancellation.
args.effects: If actual geometry permits, form a joining knot while conserving both cords and their lengths. Report measured geometry and failures. Inspection must not establish strength; only a real bounded trial may report holding, slipping or damage. Permit later untying where physically possible. The appropriate knot method is not yet known to me.

notes: The second cord's output identity and condition must come from the actual manufacture result.
A requested capability is not personal mastery; study and physical trials remain necessary.
preferences: Prefer reversible, modest-load experiments and conserve usable fiber.

projects.question: Can I undo this lightly loaded overhand knot and recover an open cord?
evidence: At tick 246 the two-round untying operation reported an untied result.
Inspection at tick 247 showed a straight cord, zero crossings, a 0.34 m centreline, condition 0.9895 and no frayed ends.
projects.uncertainty: This demonstrates one untying after one light test, not reversibility after heavy loads or repeated use; inspection also reported about 1% broken or frayed strands overall.
projects.goal: Attempt untying once and inspect the resulting geometry and condition.
completedSteps: Inspected the same cord after untying.
outputs: Recovered the same item as a straight cord, item-226-wren-2532.
projects.missing: Nothing for this bounded question.
projects.next: Keep the result as limited evidence when planning further cord work.
projects.benefit: A real trial demonstrated recovery of open cord geometry after this particular lightly loaded knot.

projects.question: Can two short reed cords be joined reversibly, and what limited load can the actual joint hold?
evidence: One owned two-ply reed cord has a measured 0.34 m centreline after untying.
My raw reed source previously passed its limited fiber-cord sample test.
projects.uncertainty: No second cord or joining result is yet established; the joining method, required tails and joint performance remain unknown.
projects.goal: Make a second cord, learn an applicable joining method, and obtain a bounded direct result without declaring a safe working load.
projects.missing: Second manufactured cord, an applicable learned method, and actual joining and test results.
projects.next: Manufacture the second cord and request a geometry-sensitive joining capability.
projects.benefit: No joining benefit demonstrated yet.

reviews.reason: Related-capability searches and the complete hand-tie-cord-knot contract establish that its only method is a single-cord overhand knot: it accepts one targetId, not two cord ends. Its non-spilling two-tail trial cannot establish the behavior of a joining bend. hand-twist-fiber-cord makes and tests cords but does not join them. Develop the missing two-cord operation in the current-conversation handoff, reusing existing cord mechanics rather than claiming their reinvention. The supplied records show a second completed cord, but their paged fragments do not establish all current geometry or whether either cord can accommodate a join. Development approval neither performs the join nor grants personal knowledge. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: No experience, pleasure, satisfaction or mastery is granted for requesting, registration, development approval, study completion alone, queries or naming. The new operation introduces no direct reward-account writes or automatic mood benefit. Emit evidence of actual completed practice, an observed join, actual untying, or a measured trial, including informative geometric failure. Only personally applicable verified information or legitimate performed practice may be considered by the existing experience evaluator; deduplicate equivalent information and physical practice across this and reused capabilities. Merely inspecting the same unchanged bend does not create new information. Any later pleasure or maintained-satisfaction integration must have explicit event eligibility, modest bounded amounts and shared functional caps, cooldown and decay in code before being enabled; none is granted by this review. Do not change protected accounts, budget, goals, permissions, nutrition or comfort; no physical-comfort benefit is claimed.
reviews.visualReview: Require reusable metadata and observable events for measured geometry, each paid crossing/pass, dressing, release, trial loading, slip, damage, break, pause, cancellation and untying. Include actor/work/join IDs, both referenced item IDs, method and law version, each cord's color and width, centerline paths, over/under crossings, bight radii, free standing spans, short-tail lengths, condition, stage and actual trial force/duration. Render two distinguishable conserved cords, not an unexplained new cord. Events and labels must distinguish incomplete, geometrically infeasible, tied-but-untested, held-at-recorded-load, slipped, jammed and broken states. An attempted crossing or failed trial must never display a success badge, proven strength or successful join. Optional annotations may show measured shortfalls without exposing hidden inventory, resources or unobserved properties. Visual presentation has no independent functional or experience effect.
reviews.specification:
Develop general operation hand-join-fiber-cords, usable by any individually trained actor with applicable owned cords. Parameters: mode attempt/inspect/trial/untie/cancel; two distinct exact cord item IDs for a new attempt; method sheet-bend for the initial version; workId for resumption; target join ID for later operations; trialForce >0 and <=10 N and trialDuration >0 and <=60 s for a trial. One capability covers construction, inspection, testing and reversal. No tools, anchors, extra fiber, second participant or automatic assistance.
References and code reuse: explicitly record reuse of hand-twist-fiber-cord, law fiber-cord@1, for conserved cord geometry, material properties, wear, extension, creep, strand damage and fragment accounting; reuse hand-tie-cord-knot, revision hand-tie-cord-knot@1, handler long.hand-tie-cord-knot, law cord-knot@1, for staged work, reservations, checks and appropriate geometric utilities. Do not reuse its one-cord topology, path formula or non-spilling assertion as a two-cord joining law. Implement a versioned joining-bend law and reusable visual schema as the missing mechanism. Reuse code is not applicant mastery; study this joining method separately. Unsupported material behavior must yield an explicit unsupported-material result, not invented strength.
Prerequisites: usable bare hands, personally completed study of this operation, two accessible owned unreserved finished cords or physically suitable finished fragments, dry safe footing and clear working space encompassing the manipulated cords. No prerequisite mastery of the two existing abilities is necessary if their mechanics are internal dependencies. Resolve actual condition, centerlines, diameter ranges, existing topology, bend limits, tails and free gripping lengths from the live items at execution, not truncated personal records or nominal length alone. Reject incompatible active knots or reservations without charge; permit separately untying them using applicable learned operations. Disclose costs before confirmation. Study costs 3 worked rounds at 0.2 energy each. Attempt costs at most 4 worked rounds at 0.5 energy each: measure/select bight and crossing, pass second end, wrap and tuck, dress and release-check. Inspection costs 1 round and 0.2 energy; trial 1 round and 0.5 energy; untying at most 2 rounds at 0.5 energy each; cancel is immediate and free. No material is consumed as a fee. Each worked manipulation round applies 0.0005 condition wear to each actually manipulated cord, once; trial additionally applies only the physical damage computed from actual load. Refusals and unworked stages charge nothing.
The initial method is a single sheet bend: make a bight in the selected cord, pass the other cord through it, around both bight legs and under its own entering part, dress with the two short ends on the same side. Choose the bight from measured cord suitability, recording the assignment; do not assume equal diameters imply equal suitability. The implementation must resolve finite-width paths and crossings, collision clearance, material bend limits and sequential hand access. A passage needs a 0.02 m clear opening and a retained 0.02 m pinch; dressing must leave each short tail at least 0.02 m plus its local cord width. Final standing parts must independently provide 0.05 m hand grips at least 0.01 m clear of the bend for the requested trial. A tie may be geometrically possible while a two-hand trial is not. Report the specific measured shortfall rather than extending a cord or silently changing method.
Maintain each cord's own centerline ledger: path inside the join plus free standing part plus free short tail equals that cord's pre-operation centerline, except for separately recorded physically computed stretch, retained creep or breakage. Knot take-up reduces useful joined span, not owned quantity. Preserve both item identities, quantities, origin and processing history; the join is a relation referencing them, not a third stock of cord. Initial tying adds no fiber and removes none. Geometric failure leaves the actually reached physical state, including a loose crossing or released bight; it does not fabricate a completed joint. The joining law must implement finite-width geometry and a material-dependent slip/retention response before execution is enabled. Use existing applicable material properties; if their friction/retention mechanism is missing, implement that minimal mechanism in this handoff, with documented parameters and bounded applicability, rather than rejecting development or inventing a strength result.
A trial pulls only the two available standing parts in opposition. Achieved force is bounded by the request, 200 N times health/100, each hand's existing grip limit of 10000 N/m times the width it grips, available span and actual failure. Resolve contact sliding, tail movement, tightening, creep, material damage and possible release or rupture for the elapsed loading interval; stop when the grip or joint fails. Reuse the existing material damage routines only within their applicability. Do not copy the overhand strength-reduction formula without establishing applicability to the bend. Record requested and achieved force, actual duration, grip slip, short-tail displacement, before/after geometry and condition, extension, strand damage, and the observed failure location. A holding event means only that this joint held that achieved force for that duration; inspection alone gives no strength, working-load rating or safety guarantee. Rupture produces owned fragments whose lengths, quantity and provenance reconcile exactly with the damaged inputs; no stock disappears or duplicates.
Each work has an exact workId, actor, input IDs, joining-law version, completed paid stages and persistent physical geometry. Reserve both items atomically before work, and block conflicting use while work or a join binds them. Auto-continuation advances only on actual worked rounds. Interrupted work, unsafe footing, lost reach, insufficient energy or obstructed space pauses before the next charge. Resume requires workId and rechecks actor, ownership, accessibility, material state, hand access and the next stage; paid stages are not repeated. Cancel releases the work reservation exactly once, preserving completed physical changes and actual topology. A complete join remains a linked assembly even after cancellation; an incomplete unretained crossing opens when unsupported, with an observable release event. Death ends active work, releases reservations once and leaves the real cords and any retained join at the death location under existing ownership rules. Neither cancellation, failure nor death refunds paid study, time, energy or wear.
Untying reverses reachable passes rather than resetting an item. It requires accessible ends, adequate condition and a physically loosenable bend; record jamming or inability to withdraw an end and retain paid progress. No guarantee of restoring original condition or undoing creep. Detached cords preserve their current lengths, damage and histories. No passive loading or strength improvement occurs merely because time passes. Existing material ageing continues while paused or joined; geometry and condition changes invalidate stale measurements. Use existing once-per-round knotted-wear accounting where applicable without double charging the same item. No maintenance materials appear automatically; upkeep is actual inspection, untying or retying with the stated costs. This version excludes unattended loads, attachments to structures and life-safety use. All validated rules execute in code without recurring model approval. Development and review waiting advance neither the world nor work.

args.name: hand-join-fiber-cords
args.function: Learn and perform a bare-hand end-to-end joining knot on two owned finished fiber cords, with inspection, bounded two-end load trials, untying and cancellation.
args.conditions: Dry safe footing and sufficient free space. I have one straight two-ply reed cord with a 0.34 m centreline, previously tied and untied, and am making a second short cord. Actual lengths, widths, condition and available gripping tails must determine whether a join is possible.
args.inputs: Two exact owned cord item IDs; a personally learned joining method; optional bounded test force and duration. No tools, anchors or added fiber are assumed.
args.costs: Learning time, working time, energy and material wear are unknown; determine and disclose them before use. Preserve paid progress and define cancellation.
args.effects: If actual geometry permits, form a joining knot while conserving both cords and their lengths. Report measured geometry and failures. Inspection must not establish strength; only a real bounded trial may report holding, slipping or damage. Permit later untying where physically possible. The appropriate knot method is not yet known to me.

projects.question: Can two short reed cords be joined reversibly, and what limited load can the actual joint hold?
evidence: At tick 263 the attempt produced a tied sheet bend between item-226-wren-2532 and item-250-wren-2847.

Untying completed at tick 267 and returned both original items.
Direct inspections at ticks 269 and 270 recorded separate straight cords with 0.34 m centrelines, zero join crossings and no partner or join id. Their recorded conditions were 0.9745 and 0.9865.

projects.goal: Document one conservative load trial and recovery of separate cords, with measured limitations.

projects.missing: Nothing for this bounded question; wider reliability remains untested.
projects.next: Retain the measured limitations when considering a practical binding application.

reviews.reason: Develop a general bare-hand crossing-binding operation, not a Wren-specific recipe. The supplied searches and registry identify cord making, an overhand knot, a two-cord sheet bend, and a woven branch screen, but none attaches two crossing rigid pieces with cord. Their load paths, inputs and effects differ: tying cord tails or joining cords does not establish cord-to-branch contact, crossing retention or branch slip. Reuse those implementations where applicable rather than redeveloping cord physics. Missing branch/contact mechanisms belong in the current-conversation development handoff. Wren has not collected the two branches; neither learning nor development supplies them. The two reported 0.34 m cords are not assumed long enough, free of existing knots or joins, or currently available from incomplete item pages. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: Evaluate information and participation separately from physical holding. Requesting, naming, registering, studying, waiting and becoming capable produce no experiential success reward. A paid measurement, informative fit failure, observed slip, or genuinely observed held trial may produce a verified personal finding with exact item/work/event references and measured conditions. Repeated identical findings are confirmations, not new information; deduplicate across probe, knot, cord-join and this operation by functional observation rather than ability name. This version grants no automatic short pleasure or satisfaction: both added amounts and caps are zero, so no new cooldown or maintenance reward process is introduced. Any future nonzero experience effect needs an explicit bounded, decaying, personally applicable rule in the existing engine, including modest familiar-practice eligibility; it is not a reason to rerun model review. No direct writes to protected reward accounts, budget, goals or permissions. Nutrition is unchanged and physical comfort gain is zero, within the global cap of 10. No other participant or their consent, communication, satisfaction or action is inferred.
reviews.visualReview: Emit observable stage-start/completion, measured-shortfall, wrap-routed, closure-tucked, release-held, release-loosened, test-start/stopped, grip-slip, crossing-slip, damage/break, pause/resume/cancel and untie-result events only when those actions occur. Provide reusable versioned metadata with work/relation ID, component IDs, actual piece transforms, crossing/contact points, cord centerline route and remaining lengths, closure crossings, visible condition, supported grip positions, stage, retention state and measured trial force/duration. Reuse existing fiber-cord, cord-knot and fragment visual components with recorded code provenance. Any schematic rendering is labeled schematic and conveys only measured or simulated supported geometry, not a strength claim. Render partial wrapping, looseness, displaced pieces, jammed closure and damage distinctly. Failed, interrupted or unimplemented contact/release stages cannot display a completed secure binding, successful trial badge, shelter overlay or strength rating. Learning alone creates no object or success event.
reviews.specification:
General operation: hand-bind-crossing, parameterized by two exact owned rigid-piece item IDs, one exact owned cord ID, crossing pose, and mode attempt/inspect/trial/untie/cancel. Initial supported method is one enclosing wrap around a two-piece crossing, closed by an overhand knot in the same cord's ends. This is a minimal experimental binding, not a rated structural lashing. Modes share one work record and contact model; do not introduce separate assessment or diagnostic abilities. Support applicable materials through registered material laws; initially use represented branch pieces and hand-twisted fiber cord. Unsupported material mechanics receive a bounded observed fit/handling precursor and a development dependency, never an invented successful binding.
Prerequisites: individually completed study; exact owned, reachable, sound enough, unreserved separate pieces; an available finished cord with accessible ends and no conflicting knot/join; dry stable footing, clear hand/work space, and feasible bare-hand positioning. No assumed tools, anchors, extra people, stock, extra cord or automatic collection. A branch-screen component is not a loose branch. Wren's item-226-wren-2532 and item-250-wren-2847 are candidate cord arguments only after authoritative current-state validation; retained join-260-wren-2978 knowledge does not establish their present availability. If joined or knotted, use the applicable existing untying operation first. One cord is sufficient as an interface input; using both as an extended assembly requires a real existing hand-join-fiber-cords result and supported routing through that join, otherwise this minimal version refuses that argument without charge.
Costs: study 4 actual rounds at 0.2 energy each, separately for every learner. Attempt reserves the three inputs and takes four paid work rounds, 0.5 energy each: measure/position; route enclosing wrap; form and tuck closure; dress and release-check. Each completed stage persists its actual geometry and measurements. Inspect costs one round and 0.2 energy; bounded trial one round and 0.5 energy, accepting force greater than 0 and at most 10 N and duration greater than 0 and at most 60 s; untie takes two rounds at 0.5 energy each, withdrawing the closure end then opening/removing the wrap. Cancel is immediate and free. No automatic work during review, study waiting, or an unworked round. Materials are retained components rather than consumable recipe units; charge actual material damage, not a fictitious stock cost.
Implementation dependencies and reuse: record source/version dependencies on hand-twist-fiber-cord and its fiber-cord@1 geometry, strength, creep and fragment handling; hand-tie-cord-knot and cord-knot@1 bend limits, overhand paths, dressing, damage and jamming; and hand-join-fiber-cords/cord-bend@1 only when validating an existing join. Record extracted shared code and modifications explicitly. Branch-screen supplies no fastening or strength law; do not transplant its windbreak effect. Add a versioned crossing-contact law in the existing development handoff: observable piece dimensions and condition, contact paths, collision clearance, available hand grips, routing feasibility, wrap tension, frictional slip and release behavior. Existing reed friction assumptions may be reused only for their applicable contact pair; cord-to-branch friction and branch bending/break response require an explicit supported law or actual bounded measurement. They are not inferred from cord-to-cord friction.
Execution: obtain represented or physically measured local dimensions and branch condition through paid handling; do not invent dimensions from the generic word branch. Store piece transforms, crossing angle, contact locations and accessible ends. Compute the wrap centerline around the actual crossing with material bend limits and hand/passage clearance. Cord centerline equals routed wrap plus closure path plus both tails and any remaining slack; it may not exceed the available measured centerline. Use cord-knot@1 closure constraints, including pinch and retained-tail allowances; do not merely subtract two branch circumferences or assume a 0.34 m fit. Each stage checks whether one person can hold and route the pieces with the hands actually available. No invisible third hand or fixed anchor. An infeasible route or insufficient length produces a paid, measured shortfall at the stage where discovered and no completed binding.
Dressing and releasing must execute supported closure retention and contact mechanics. A released wrap that opens, loosens or lets either branch escape is failed or loose, not successfully bound. If retained, create a relation referencing the original three item IDs and their geometry, without copying items, quantities, ownership or cord length. Installed pieces remain conserved components and cannot simultaneously be consumed, separately carried away or assigned to another work. The relation moves only as the actual assembly permits and counts the original material load once. It grants no shelter, usable anchor, furniture, strength rating, health, warmth or comfort effect.
A trial needs a real opposed hand-grip pair on the pieces, clear of the crossing; one hand must not be silently replaced by a fixture. Specify grip sites and force direction. Apply only the minimum of requested force, existing actor/grip limits, and any conservative supported test limit; record the actual force history and duration, not merely requested values. Resolve cord extension/creep, closure behavior, contact slip, relative piece motion and material damage using the registered laws, stopping on loss of grip, slip, breakage or unsafe geometry. Refuse unsupported load modes rather than declaring a pass. A held result means only that particular arrangement, force and time. Inspection reports visible routing, closure, slack, displacement and damage, not hidden strength. Untying can fail or jam under cord-knot@1; no forced restoration to pristine cord.
Conservation and lifecycle: preserve item IDs, material amounts, origin, existing wear and cord centerline through all stages. Breakage produces conserved fragments or damaged piece records, never replacements. During partial work keep only genuine supported geometry; anything needing the actor's continuing grip relaxes on interruption. Low energy, leaving reach, changed footing, conflicting use or missing clearance pauses before charging the next stage. Resume by workId revalidates state and continues from the last physically surviving stage; paid history remains even if a relaxed route must be redone. Cancel releases unused reservations once and leaves worked material and actual retained geometry where they are. A retained completed binding remains a relation, not a permanently reserved job. Death stops work, removes hand support, resolves relaxation and leaves materials and any retained relation at the location under ordinary ownership/death rules. No paid time, energy, wear or damage is refunded; unused material is released, not recreated. Completed untying removes the relation and releases the same components.
Ongoing behavior and maintenance: no continuing hand tension after release. Apply existing ageing and environmental wear once to the original components. Actual subsequent movement, handling or loading must resolve through the crossing-contact law and update slack, slip and retention; unsupported loads have no certified holding effect. Loss of retention immediately changes the relation to loose or separated and removes any constrained motion. Inspection does not repair anything. Maintenance in this version consists of inspection, an actual untying attempt, and a fresh paid binding attempt using available components; no automatic tightening, healing or free replacement. Until the contact model and release check are executable, expose only paid fit/routing observations, leave the work explicitly incomplete, and retain the missing mechanism in the same development handoff rather than claiming completion.

reviews.reason: The retrieved hand-twist-fiber-cord schema limits requestedLength to 0.30 m; it cannot execute the requested continuous cord up to 0.60 m through its existing arguments. Hand-join-fiber-cords instead creates a knotted relation between two cords, not a longer uninterrupted two-ply cord, and hand-bind-crossing explicitly excludes joined cords. Develop a parameterized extension of the existing cord-making operation in the current-conversation handoff, recording code reuse rather than claiming reinvention. The supplied observations justify attempting and measuring a longer cord, not guaranteeing its production or a successful binding. Development waiting advances no world time. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: Study individually for 3 rounds at 0.2 energy per round if the applicable capability is not already learned; verified personal learning may be migrated without granting mastery merely from observations. Study, requesting, registration, inspection queries and naming give no experience reward. Keep the existing no-reward behavior for this smallest functional extension: it adds no pleasure, satisfaction, comfort or nutrition effect. Record observable practice and genuinely new measured outcomes, including informative failures, separately from rewards; repeated geometry reports are not new information. Any later experience integration must use real personally applicable events, functional deduplication, bounded awards/caps, decay and cooldown in code, and may recognize modest familiar legitimate practice without requiring novelty. Never modify protected reward accounts, budgets, goals or permissions; physical comfort remains capped at 10 and mood never reduces basic nutrition.
reviews.visualReview: Emit reusable stage-progress, pause, resume, cancellation, measured-shortfall, release-result, inspection and trial events with actor ID, work/item references, revision, stage/section, paid progress, measured lengths, ply diameter, condition, actual outcome and visible material/scrap allocation. Reuse the existing fiber-cord visual representation with parameterized two-ply geometry, S/Z twist, loose ends and completion state. Display only the currently supported geometry: held or partially plied fiber must remain visibly unfinished, and failed release or shortfall cannot show a completed 0.60 m cord. A completed cord is marked untested until an actual trial; no strength badge, successful binding, hidden-resource preview or reward animation follows merely from development, study or a request.
reviews.specification:
Extend hand-twist-fiber-cord, handler long.hand-twist-fiber-cord, revision hand-twist-fiber-cord@1, using fiber-cord@1 material, geometry, damage, sampling, ownership and trial code. Retain sample/make/inspect/trial/cancel modes; increase requestedLength's maximum to 0.60 m, retaining minimum 0.05 m and exact materials[{stackId,quantity}] and workId arguments. This is a general operation for any applicable actor, fiber source and quantity, not a Wren-only interface. Preserve old work records and their paid progress under their recorded revision; do not silently restart or reinterpret them. Dependencies are the existing cord handler, reed strand law, personal passing-source-sample records, item reservation and persistent work/event systems. No tool, anchor, water, extra fiber, splice, or strength enhancement is supplied. Only materials supported by an executable strand law can proceed; unsupported material is a reported mechanism gap, not a fabricated result.
Require exact owned, accessible, unreserved stacks totaling 0.2–1 unit in 0.1 steps, one fiber and source, with processing/condition covered by the actor's passing sample under the existing 0.05 tolerance. A known observation of successful cord making is not automatically mastery or a matching sample. item-225-wren-2518 is a tested-lot record to validate, not a grant of additional raw stock. Existing finished cords item-226-wren-2532 and item-250-wren-2847 cannot be reclassified as raw fiber or silently extended. Validate the supplied raw stack IDs at execution; do not infer the contents of unread inventory records. Require dry footing, sufficient clear working space and nobody within the actor's radius plus half the working cord length. Check actual hand reach, grip and ability to retain intermediate twist without external assistance. Bare-hand sequential regripping may proceed only where the implemented geometry can retain the work; otherwise pause or record the measured limitation, never assume an anchor.
For requested twisted length L, use n=ceil(L/0.30) work sections, each at most 0.30 m, with continuous strands rather than joins. Charge n separate-align rounds, n twist rounds, n counter-ply rounds and one final release-check round, each 1 energy and one world round: 4 rounds/4 energy through 0.30 m, 7 rounds/7 energy above 0.30 through 0.60 m. Store section endpoints, actual aligned/twisted/plied lengths, held versus released geometry, stage, material allocation, condition and paid charges in the work record. Round 1 measures feasibility; charge this real attempted work even if it discovers a shortfall, but charge no unperformed later rounds. Preserve the existing 0.0005 condition loss per actual worked round, once, and its condition-at-least-0.5 release requirement. Sample remains 0.1 owned non-food unit, 1 round/0.5 energy, producing a tested lot or cracked scrap; inspect remains 1 round/0.2 energy; trial remains 1 round/0.5 energy with the existing force, duration and item limits; cancellation is free. Invalid requests cost nothing.
Derive solid volume from the actual selected material under fiber-cord@1, retaining reed's 1.8 m stems, 500 kg/m3 density, water-share treatment, wet strength and creep rather than inventing another material law. Divide actual usable solid volume equally between two plies using the existing twist take-up factor 1.155 and 0.02 m loose-end allowance. Require strand lengths sufficient for the computed ply paths, diameters within 1–12 mm, and feasible hand handling. Preserve exact length semantics: requested twisted span is not overall length including loose ends. More length at fixed usable volume means thinner plies, not free material. Record actual diameter, twisted length, overall length, condition, strand losses and twist directions. Allocate every input quantity exactly once among reserved unworked material, workpiece, returned fiber and broken scrap; volume in finished plies plus ends and scraps cannot exceed input volume. No rounding creates stock. On measured infeasibility return recoverable fiber and retain any real damage as scrap; do not label a short or incomplete piece as the requested completed product.
A completed release check creates only the supported, owned, untested cord. A shortfall reports supported dimensions and the limiting constraint; accepting any shorter unfinished work for further processing requires an explicit subsequent action. Inspect exposes only measured work/item geometry. Trial reuses fiber-cord@1 force, grip, extension, creep, damage and fragment accounting and proves only the actual force and duration. The reported 0.4332 m binding requirement is evidence for that earlier geometry, not a universal target or promise: a longer thinner cord changes width and bend geometry. Any later binding must independently execute hand-bind-crossing with exact items and recompute its wrap, closure, tails and retention under crossing-contact@1, cord-knot@1 and cord-bend@1.
Unworked rounds, insufficient energy, lost reach, unsafe footing or obstructed workspace pause before charging. Paid stage progress persists; hand-held tension may relax, and resume rechecks the physical state without claiming completion of lost twist. Any necessary real rework is explicitly charged as work, not a second charge for an unchanged completed stage. Resume with make and workId only; reject conflicting material or length arguments. Cancel or death releases unworked reservations exactly once and leaves allocated workpiece and scrap in their actual state and location; death leaves materials at the death location. Never refund spent time, energy or worked material. No automatic background fabrication runs while paused or during development. Finished cord retains ordinary material wear and any existing ongoing trial or binding processes; this extension adds no automatic repair, maintenance benefit or indefinite retained tension. All validation, accounting, state transitions and deduplication must execute in code rather than renewed model review.
